english_rwwad.text: Pharaoh said, “Then what about the former [disbelieving] nations?”

verses.translation: Pharaoh said, “Then what about the former [disbelieving] nations?”

verses.arabic: قَالَ عِلْمُهَا عِندَ رَبِّى فِى كِتَٰبٍ لَّا يَضِلُّ رَبِّى وَلَا يَنسَى

english_rwwad.text: He said, “Its knowledge is with my Lord in a Record. My Lord never errs, nor does He forget.”

verses.translation: He said, “Its knowledge is with my Lord in a Record. My Lord never errs, nor does He forget.”

verses.arabic: ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلْأَرْضَ مَهْدًا وَسَلَكَ لَكُمْ فِيهَا سُبُلًا وَأَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِۦٓ أَزْوَٰجًا مِّن نَّبَاتٍ شَتَّىٰ

english_rwwad.text: It is He Who spread out the earth for you and made therein pathways for you, and sent down rain from the sky; and We brought forth thereby various types of plants.

verses.translation: It is He Who spread out the earth for you and made therein pathways for you, and sent down rain from the sky; and We brought forth thereby various types of plants.

verses.arabic: كُلُوا۟ وَٱرْعَوْا۟ أَنْعَٰمَكُمْ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَـَٔايَٰتٍ لِّأُو۟لِى ٱلنُّهَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: Eat and graze your livestock. Indeed, there are signs in this for people of sound intellect.

verses.translation: Eat and graze your livestock. Indeed, there are signs in this for people of sound intellect.

verses.arabic: مِنْهَا خَلَقْنَٰكُمْ وَفِيهَا نُعِيدُكُمْ وَمِنْهَا نُخْرِجُكُمْ تَارَةً أُخْرَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: From this [earth] We created you, and to it We will return you, and from it We will raise you once again.

verses.translation: From this [earth] We created you, and to it We will return you, and from it We will raise you once again.

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ أَرَيْنَٰهُ ءَايَٰتِنَا كُلَّهَا فَكَذَّبَ وَأَبَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: We showed Pharaoh all Our signs, but he rejected them and refused to believe.

verses.translation: We showed Pharaoh all Our signs, but he rejected them and refused to believe.

verses.arabic: قَالَ أَجِئْتَنَا لِتُخْرِجَنَا مِنْ أَرْضِنَا بِسِحْرِكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: He said, “Have you come to drive us out of our land with your magic, O Moses?

verses.translation: He said, “Have you come to drive us out of our land with your magic, O Moses?

verses.arabic: فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّكَ بِسِحْرٍ مِّثْلِهِۦ فَٱجْعَلْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكَ مَوْعِدًا لَّا نُخْلِفُهُۥ نَحْنُ وَلَآ أَنتَ مَكَانًا سُوًى

english_rwwad.text: We will surely bring you similar magic. So appoint a day between us that neither you nor we will fail to keep, in a convenient place[1].”
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] i.e., a midway place between us.

verses.translation: We will surely bring you similar magic. So appoint a day between us that neither you nor we will fail to keep, in a convenient place[1].”

verses.arabic: قَالَ مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ ٱلزِّينَةِ وَأَن يُحْشَرَ ٱلنَّاسُ ضُحًى

english_rwwad.text: Moses said, “Your appointment is the festival day[1]; let the people be gathered at forenoon[2].”
english_rwwad.footnotes:
[1] So that more people could witness the event.
 [2] So that people could see Allah’s signs clearly.

verses.translation: Moses said, “Your appointment is the festival day[1]; let the people be gathered at forenoon[2].”

verses.arabic: فَتَوَلَّىٰ فِرْعَوْنُ فَجَمَعَ كَيْدَهُۥ ثُمَّ أَتَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: So Pharaoh went away and put together his scheme, then came forth.

verses.translation: So Pharaoh went away and put together his scheme, then came forth.

verses.arabic: قَالَ لَهُم مُّوسَىٰ وَيْلَكُمْ لَا تَفْتَرُوا۟ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبًا فَيُسْحِتَكُم بِعَذَابٍ وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنِ ٱفْتَرَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: Moses said to them, “Woe to you, do not fabricate lies against Allah[1], lest He exterminate you with a punishment. Those who fabricate lies are bound to fail.”
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] By considering Allah’s miracles as magic.

verses.translation: Moses said to them, “Woe to you, do not fabricate lies against Allah[1], lest He exterminate you with a punishment. Those who fabricate lies are bound to fail.”

verses.arabic: فَتَنَٰزَعُوٓا۟ أَمْرَهُم بَيْنَهُمْ وَأَسَرُّوا۟ ٱلنَّجْوَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: Then they disputed the matter among themselves and kept their talk private.

verses.translation: Then they disputed the matter among themselves and kept their talk private.

verses.arabic: قَالُوٓا۟ إِنْ هَٰذَٰنِ لَسَٰحِرَٰنِ يُرِيدَانِ أَن يُخْرِجَاكُم مِّنْ أَرْضِكُم بِسِحْرِهِمَا وَيَذْهَبَا بِطَرِيقَتِكُمُ ٱلْمُثْلَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: They said, “These two are merely magicians who want to drive you out of your land with their magic and destroy your exemplary way of life.

verses.translation: They said, “These two are merely magicians who want to drive you out of your land with their magic and destroy your exemplary way of life.

verses.arabic: فَأَجْمِعُوا۟ كَيْدَكُمْ ثُمَّ ٱئْتُوا۟ صَفًّا وَقَدْ أَفْلَحَ ٱلْيَوْمَ مَنِ ٱسْتَعْلَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: So gather your scheme, then line up in a row. Whoever prevails today is indeed the victor.”

verses.translation: So gather your scheme, then line up in a row. Whoever prevails today is indeed the victor.”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِمَّآ أَن تُلْقِىَ وَإِمَّآ أَن نَّكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَلْقَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: They said, “O Moses, either you throw or shall we be the first to throw!”

verses.translation: They said, “O Moses, either you throw or shall we be the first to throw!”

verses.arabic: قَالَ بَلْ أَلْقُوا۟ فَإِذَا حِبَالُهُمْ وَعِصِيُّهُمْ يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ مِن سِحْرِهِمْ أَنَّهَا تَسْعَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: He said, “No; you throw first.” Suddenly their ropes and staffs appeared to him, owing to their magic, as if they were slithering.

verses.translation: He said, “No; you throw first.” Suddenly their ropes and staffs appeared to him, owing to their magic, as if they were slithering.

verses.arabic: فَأَوْجَسَ فِى نَفْسِهِۦ خِيفَةً مُّوسَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: Then Moses sensed fear within himself.

verses.translation: Then Moses sensed fear within himself.

verses.arabic: قُلْنَا لَا تَخَفْ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: We said, “Do not be afraid; it is you who will prevail.

verses.translation: We said, “Do not be afraid; it is you who will prevail.

verses.arabic: وَأَلْقِ مَا فِى يَمِينِكَ تَلْقَفْ مَا صَنَعُوٓا۟ إِنَّمَا صَنَعُوا۟ كَيْدُ سَٰحِرٍ وَلَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلسَّاحِرُ حَيْثُ أَتَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: Throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow up what they have contrived. They have only contrived a magic trick, and the magician will never prosper, wherever he goes.”

verses.translation: Throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow up what they have contrived. They have only contrived a magic trick, and the magician will never prosper, wherever he goes.”

verses.arabic: فَأُلْقِىَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ سُجَّدًا قَالُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّ هَٰرُونَ وَمُوسَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: So the magicians fell down in prostration[1], saying, “We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.”
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] They realized that the miracles of Moses were not impressions of magic, but absolute realities.

verses.translation: So the magicians fell down in prostration[1], saying, “We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ ءَامَنتُمْ لَهُۥ قَبْلَ أَنْ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمْ إِنَّهُۥ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ ٱلَّذِى عَلَّمَكُمُ ٱلسِّحْرَ فَلَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُم مِّنْ خِلَٰفٍ وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ فِى جُذُوعِ ٱلنَّخْلِ وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ أَيُّنَآ أَشَدُّ عَذَابًا وَأَبْقَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: Pharaoh said, “How dare you believe in him before I give you permission! He must be your master who taught you magic! I will surely cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, and I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees; you will surely know whose punishment is more severe and more lasting!”

verses.translation: Pharaoh said, “How dare you believe in him before I give you permission! He must be your master who taught you magic! I will surely cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, and I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees; you will surely know whose punishment is more severe and more lasting!”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ لَن نُّؤْثِرَكَ عَلَىٰ مَا جَآءَنَا مِنَ ٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ وَٱلَّذِى فَطَرَنَا فَٱقْضِ مَآ أَنتَ قَاضٍ إِنَّمَا تَقْضِى هَٰذِهِ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَآ

english_rwwad.text: They said, “We will never prefer you over the clear signs that have come to us, or over the One Who created us[1]. So decide whatever you will. You can only make a decision about the life of this world.
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] It can also be interpreted as an oath, i.e., “By the One Who created us, we will never prefer you over...”.

verses.translation: They said, “We will never prefer you over the clear signs that have come to us, or over the One Who created us[1]. So decide whatever you will. You can only make a decision about the life of this world.

verses.arabic: إِنَّآ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّنَا لِيَغْفِرَ لَنَا خَطَٰيَٰنَا وَمَآ أَكْرَهْتَنَا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ ٱلسِّحْرِ وَٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰٓ

english_rwwad.text: We surely believe in our Lord so that He may forgive us our sins and the magic that you have compelled us to practice, for Allah is best [in reward] and more lasting [in punishment].”

verses.translation: We surely believe in our Lord so that He may forgive us our sins and the magic that you have compelled us to practice, for Allah is best [in reward] and more lasting [in punishment].”

verses.arabic: إِنَّهُۥ مَن يَأْتِ رَبَّهُۥ مُجْرِمًا فَإِنَّ لَهُۥ جَهَنَّمَ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحْيَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: Whoever comes to his Lord as an evildoer, for him is Hell; he will neither die therein nor live[1].
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] He will neither die to relax from punishment, nor live a pleasant life.

verses.translation: Whoever comes to his Lord as an evildoer, for him is Hell; he will neither die therein nor live[1].

verses.arabic: وَمَن يَأْتِهِۦ مُؤْمِنًا قَدْ عَمِلَ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمُ ٱلدَّرَجَٰتُ ٱلْعُلَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: But whoever comes to Him as a believer, having done righteous deeds, it is they who will have the highest ranks:

verses.translation: But whoever comes to Him as a believer, having done righteous deeds, it is they who will have the highest ranks:

verses.arabic: جَنَّٰتُ عَدْنٍ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا وَذَٰلِكَ جَزَآءُ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ

english_rwwad.text: Gardens of Eternity, under which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Such is the reward of those who purify themselves[1].
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] From disbelief and sins.

verses.translation: Gardens of Eternity, under which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Such is the reward of those who purify themselves[1].

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَسْرِ بِعِبَادِى فَٱضْرِبْ لَهُمْ طَرِيقًا فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ يَبَسًا لَّا تَخَٰفُ دَرَكًا وَلَا تَخْشَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: We inspired Moses, “Travel by night with My slaves, and strike for them a dry path across the sea. Have no fear of being overtaken, nor be afraid [of drowning].”

verses.translation: We inspired Moses, “Travel by night with My slaves, and strike for them a dry path across the sea. Have no fear of being overtaken, nor be afraid [of drowning].”

verses.arabic: فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ فِرْعَوْنُ بِجُنُودِهِۦ فَغَشِيَهُم مِّنَ ٱلْيَمِّ مَا غَشِيَهُمْ

english_rwwad.text: Then Pharaoh pursued them with his soldiers, but they were completely overwhelmed by the sea[1].
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] i.e., not only drowning in water but other things which are only known to Allah such as terror, pain, regret, etc.

verses.translation: Then Pharaoh pursued them with his soldiers, but they were completely overwhelmed by the sea[1].

verses.arabic: وَأَضَلَّ فِرْعَوْنُ قَوْمَهُۥ وَمَا هَدَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: Thus Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide them.

verses.translation: Thus Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide them.

verses.arabic: يَٰبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ قَدْ أَنجَيْنَٰكُم مِّنْ عَدُوِّكُمْ وَوَٰعَدْنَٰكُمْ جَانِبَ ٱلطُّورِ ٱلْأَيْمَنَ وَنَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْمَنَّ وَٱلسَّلْوَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: O Children of Israel, We rescued you from your enemy, and made an appointment with you[1] on the right side of Mount Tūr [in Sinai], and sent down for you manna and quails[2],
english_rwwad.footnotes:
[1] i.e., with your prophet to talk to him and receive the Tablets for your guidance.
 [2] They were provided with manna (bread or honey-like food) and quails in the wilderness after they left Egypt.

verses.translation: O Children of Israel, We rescued you from your enemy, and made an appointment with you[1] on the right side of Mount Tūr [in Sinai], and sent down for you manna and quails[2],

verses.arabic: كُلُوا۟ مِن طَيِّبَٰتِ مَا رَزَقْنَٰكُمْ وَلَا تَطْغَوْا۟ فِيهِ فَيَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبِى وَمَن يَحْلِلْ عَلَيْهِ غَضَبِى فَقَدْ هَوَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: [saying], “Eat from the good things We have provided for you, but do not exceed the limits therein, or My wrath will befall you, for anyone upon whom My wrath befalls has surely perished.

verses.translation: [saying], “Eat from the good things We have provided for you, but do not exceed the limits therein, or My wrath will befall you, for anyone upon whom My wrath befalls has surely perished.

verses.arabic: وَإِنِّى لَغَفَّارٌ لِّمَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًا ثُمَّ ٱهْتَدَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: I am indeed Most Forgiving to those who repent and believe, and do righteous deeds, then stay on the right path.”

verses.translation: I am indeed Most Forgiving to those who repent and believe, and do righteous deeds, then stay on the right path.”

verses.arabic: وَمَآ أَعْجَلَكَ عَن قَوْمِكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: [Allah asked], “What made you hasten from your people, O Moses?”[1]
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] Moses chose a delegation of seventy people from the Children of Israel to go to Mount Tūr to receive the Tablets. He was in haste to meet his Lord, so he rushed to the appointment and arrived before his people, leaving them behind. See (7:143-145)

verses.translation: [Allah asked], “What made you hasten from your people, O Moses?”[1]

verses.arabic: قَالَ هُمْ أُو۟لَآءِ عَلَىٰٓ أَثَرِى وَعَجِلْتُ إِلَيْكَ رَبِّ لِتَرْضَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: He said, “They are following my footsteps; I hastened to You, my Lord, to please You.”

verses.translation: He said, “They are following my footsteps; I hastened to You, my Lord, to please You.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ فَإِنَّا قَدْ فَتَنَّا قَوْمَكَ مِنۢ بَعْدِكَ وَأَضَلَّهُمُ ٱلسَّامِرِىُّ

english_rwwad.text: Allah said, “We have certainly tested your people in your absence, and Sāmiri[1] has led them astray.”
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] i.e., the Samaritan (a man from Samaria), a hypocrite who led the Children of Israel to the worship of the calf, or to idol-worship.

verses.translation: Allah said, “We have certainly tested your people in your absence, and Sāmiri[1] has led them astray.”

verses.arabic: فَرَجَعَ مُوسَىٰٓ إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ غَضْبَٰنَ أَسِفًا قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ أَلَمْ يَعِدْكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ وَعْدًا حَسَنًا أَفَطَالَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْعَهْدُ أَمْ أَرَدتُّمْ أَن يَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ فَأَخْلَفْتُم مَّوْعِدِى

english_rwwad.text: So Moses returned to his people, angry and sorrowful. He said, “O my people, did your Lord not promise you a good promise[1]? Was my absence too long for you, or did you want the wrath from your Lord to befall you, so you broke your promise to me[2]?”
english_rwwad.footnotes:
[1] To send down the Torah for your guidance.
 [2] Of worshiping Allah alone until Moses comes back to them.

verses.translation: So Moses returned to his people, angry and sorrowful. He said, “O my people, did your Lord not promise you a good promise[1]? Was my absence too long for you, or did you want the wrath from your Lord to befall you, so you broke your promise to me[2]?”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ مَآ أَخْلَفْنَا مَوْعِدَكَ بِمَلْكِنَا وَلَٰكِنَّا حُمِّلْنَآ أَوْزَارًا مِّن زِينَةِ ٱلْقَوْمِ فَقَذَفْنَٰهَا فَكَذَٰلِكَ أَلْقَى ٱلسَّامِرِىُّ

english_rwwad.text: They said, “We did not break our promise to you out of our own free will, but we were made to carry loads of the people’s jewelry, so we threw them [into the fire], and so did the Sāmiri throw.”[1]
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] They carried loads of jewelry of the people of the Pharaoh that they had with them, so they threw them into the fire in order to get rid of them. As for the Sāmiri, he threw the dust that he collected from the hoof-print of Gabriel’s horse.

verses.translation: They said, “We did not break our promise to you out of our own free will, but we were made to carry loads of the people’s jewelry, so we threw them [into the fire], and so did the Sāmiri throw.”[1]

verses.arabic: فَأَخْرَجَ لَهُمْ عِجْلًا جَسَدًا لَّهُۥ خُوَارٌ فَقَالُوا۟ هَٰذَآ إِلَٰهُكُمْ وَإِلَٰهُ مُوسَىٰ فَنَسِىَ

english_rwwad.text: Then he molded for them an image of a calf that made a mooing sound. They said, “This is your god and Moses’ god, but he has forgotten.”

verses.translation: Then he molded for them an image of a calf that made a mooing sound. They said, “This is your god and Moses’ god, but he has forgotten.”

verses.arabic: أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَلَّا يَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِمْ قَوْلًا وَلَا يَمْلِكُ لَهُمْ ضَرًّا وَلَا نَفْعًا

english_rwwad.text: Do they not see that it does not respond a word to them, nor does it have the power to harm or benefit them?

verses.translation: Do they not see that it does not respond a word to them, nor does it have the power to harm or benefit them?

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ قَالَ لَهُمْ هَٰرُونُ مِن قَبْلُ يَٰقَوْمِ إِنَّمَا فُتِنتُم بِهِۦ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ فَٱتَّبِعُونِى وَأَطِيعُوٓا۟ أَمْرِى

english_rwwad.text: Aaron told them beforehand, “O my people, you are being tested with it. Your Lord is the Most Compassionate, so follow me and obey my command.”

verses.translation: Aaron told them beforehand, “O my people, you are being tested with it. Your Lord is the Most Compassionate, so follow me and obey my command.”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ لَن نَّبْرَحَ عَلَيْهِ عَٰكِفِينَ حَتَّىٰ يَرْجِعَ إِلَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: They said, “We will never cease to worship it until Moses comes back to us.”

verses.translation: They said, “We will never cease to worship it until Moses comes back to us.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ يَٰهَٰرُونُ مَا مَنَعَكَ إِذْ رَأَيْتَهُمْ ضَلُّوٓا۟

english_rwwad.text: Moses said, “O Aaron, what prevented you when you saw them going astray,

verses.translation: Moses said, “O Aaron, what prevented you when you saw them going astray,

verses.arabic: أَلَّا تَتَّبِعَنِ أَفَعَصَيْتَ أَمْرِى

english_rwwad.text: from following me? Did you disobey my command?”[1]

verses.translation: from following me? Did you disobey my command?”[1]

verses.arabic: قَالَ يَبْنَؤُمَّ لَا تَأْخُذْ بِلِحْيَتِى وَلَا بِرَأْسِىٓ إِنِّى خَشِيتُ أَن تَقُولَ فَرَّقْتَ بَيْنَ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ وَلَمْ تَرْقُبْ قَوْلِى

english_rwwad.text: Aaron said, “O son of my mother, do not seize me by my beard or by my head! I feared that you would say, ‘You have caused division among the Children of Israel, and did not heed my words.’”

verses.translation: Aaron said, “O son of my mother, do not seize me by my beard or by my head! I feared that you would say, ‘You have caused division among the Children of Israel, and did not heed my words.’”

verses.arabic: قَالَ فَمَا خَطْبُكَ يَٰسَٰمِرِىُّ

english_rwwad.text: Moses said, “What is the matter with you, O Sāmiri?”

verses.translation: Moses said, “What is the matter with you, O Sāmiri?”

verses.arabic: قَالَ بَصُرْتُ بِمَا لَمْ يَبْصُرُوا۟ بِهِۦ فَقَبَضْتُ قَبْضَةً مِّنْ أَثَرِ ٱلرَّسُولِ فَنَبَذْتُهَا وَكَذَٰلِكَ سَوَّلَتْ لِى نَفْسِى

english_rwwad.text: He said, “I saw something they did not see, so I took a handful [of dust] from the hoof-print of the horse of the messenger [Gabriel] and cast it [into the fire][1]. This is what my mind prompted me.”
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] While Moses and the Children of Israel were crossing the sea, the Sāmiri saw Gabriel on a horse leading the way, so he took a handful of dust from the hoof-prints of his horse and later threw it at the calf that was made out of the melted ornaments so it started making a bellowing sound.

verses.translation: He said, “I saw something they did not see, so I took a handful [of dust] from the hoof-print of the horse of the messenger [Gabriel] and cast it [into the fire][1]. This is what my mind prompted me.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ فَٱذْهَبْ فَإِنَّ لَكَ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ أَن تَقُولَ لَا مِسَاسَ وَإِنَّ لَكَ مَوْعِدًا لَّن تُخْلَفَهُۥ وَٱنظُرْ إِلَىٰٓ إِلَٰهِكَ ٱلَّذِى ظَلْتَ عَلَيْهِ عَاكِفًا لَّنُحَرِّقَنَّهُۥ ثُمَّ لَنَنسِفَنَّهُۥ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ نَسْفًا

english_rwwad.text: Moses said, “Begone then! Your [punishment] in this life will be to say, ‘Do not touch me,’[1] but there awaits you an appointed time for your reckoning that you cannot escape[2]. Now look at your so-called god which you kept worshiping; We will surely burn it and then scatter it in the sea.
english_rwwad.footnotes:
[1] So he was completely shunned by all people, alienated in the desert.
 [2] On the Day of Judgment.

verses.translation: Moses said, “Begone then! Your [punishment] in this life will be to say, ‘Do not touch me,’[1] but there awaits you an appointed time for your reckoning that you cannot escape[2]. Now look at your so-called god which you kept worshiping; We will surely burn it and then scatter it in the sea.

verses.arabic: إِنَّمَآ إِلَٰهُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَسِعَ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ عِلْمًا

english_rwwad.text: [O people], your god is only Allah; none has the right to be worshiped except Him. He encompasses everything in knowledge.”

verses.translation: [O people], your god is only Allah; none has the right to be worshiped except Him. He encompasses everything in knowledge.”

verses.arabic: كَذَٰلِكَ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ أَنۢبَآءِ مَا قَدْ سَبَقَ وَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَٰكَ مِن لَّدُنَّا ذِكْرًا

english_rwwad.text: This is how We relate to you [O Prophet] from the stories of the past, and We have given you a Reminder[1] from Us.
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] i.e., the Qur’an.

verses.translation: This is how We relate to you [O Prophet] from the stories of the past, and We have given you a Reminder[1] from Us.

verses.arabic: مَّنْ أَعْرَضَ عَنْهُ فَإِنَّهُۥ يَحْمِلُ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ وِزْرًا

english_rwwad.text: Whoever turns away from it will bear a heavy burden on the Day of Resurrection,

verses.translation: Whoever turns away from it will bear a heavy burden on the Day of Resurrection,

verses.arabic: خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهِ وَسَآءَ لَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ حِمْلًا

english_rwwad.text: abiding therein forever[1]. What a terrible burden they will carry on the Day of Resurrection!
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] i.e., in the state of sin and punishment.

verses.translation: abiding therein forever[1]. What a terrible burden they will carry on the Day of Resurrection!

verses.arabic: يَوْمَ يُنفَخُ فِى ٱلصُّورِ وَنَحْشُرُ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ يَوْمَئِذٍ زُرْقًا

english_rwwad.text: the Day when the Trumpet will be blown; on that Day We will gather together the wicked sightless[1] [from horror].
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] i.e., blind, blue-eyed, blue-faced out of terror.

verses.translation: the Day when the Trumpet will be blown; on that Day We will gather together the wicked sightless[1] [from horror].

verses.arabic: يَتَخَٰفَتُونَ بَيْنَهُمْ إِن لَّبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا عَشْرًا

english_rwwad.text: They will whisper to one another, “You stayed no more than ten days [on earth].”

verses.translation: They will whisper to one another, “You stayed no more than ten days [on earth].”

verses.arabic: نَّحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يَقُولُونَ إِذْ يَقُولُ أَمْثَلُهُمْ طَرِيقَةً إِن لَّبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا يَوْمًا

english_rwwad.text: We know best what they will say – the most discerning among them will say, “You stayed no more than a day.”

verses.translation: We know best what they will say – the most discerning among them will say, “You stayed no more than a day.”

verses.arabic: وَيَسْـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلْجِبَالِ فَقُلْ يَنسِفُهَا رَبِّى نَسْفًا

english_rwwad.text: They ask you about the mountains, say, “My Lord will scatter them into dust,

verses.translation: They ask you about the mountains, say, “My Lord will scatter them into dust,

verses.arabic: فَيَذَرُهَا قَاعًا صَفْصَفًا

english_rwwad.text: and He will leave the earth level and plain,

verses.translation: and He will leave the earth level and plain,

verses.arabic: لَّا تَرَىٰ فِيهَا عِوَجًا وَلَآ أَمْتًا

english_rwwad.text: you will not see therein any troughs or peaks.”

verses.translation: you will not see therein any troughs or peaks.”

verses.arabic: يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَّبِعُونَ ٱلدَّاعِىَ لَا عِوَجَ لَهُۥ وَخَشَعَتِ ٱلْأَصْوَاتُ لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ فَلَا تَسْمَعُ إِلَّا هَمْسًا

english_rwwad.text: On that day, they will follow the summoner[1]; none will dare to deviate. All voices will be hushed in awe before the Most Compassionate; you will hear nothing except a whisper[2].
english_rwwad.footnotes:
[1] To the gathering for reckoning.
 [2] Or the sound of footsteps.

verses.translation: On that day, they will follow the summoner[1]; none will dare to deviate. All voices will be hushed in awe before the Most Compassionate; you will hear nothing except a whisper[2].

verses.arabic: يَوْمَئِذٍ لَّا تَنفَعُ ٱلشَّفَٰعَةُ إِلَّا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ وَرَضِىَ لَهُۥ قَوْلًا

english_rwwad.text: On that day, no intercession will be of any use except to whom the Most Compassionate gave permission and approved his word.

verses.translation: On that day, no intercession will be of any use except to whom the Most Compassionate gave permission and approved his word.

verses.arabic: يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِهِۦ عِلْمًا

english_rwwad.text: He knows all that is ahead of them and all that is behind them[1], but they do not encompass it[2] with their knowledge.
english_rwwad.footnotes:
[1] i.e., what awaits them in the Hereafter and what they did in the world.
 [2] i.e., His knowledge.

verses.translation: He knows all that is ahead of them and all that is behind them[1], but they do not encompass it[2] with their knowledge.

verses.arabic: وَعَنَتِ ٱلْوُجُوهُ لِلْحَىِّ ٱلْقَيُّومِ وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنْ حَمَلَ ظُلْمًا

english_rwwad.text: All faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, Self-Sustaining. Those burdened with wrongdoing[1] will be in a total loss.
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] i.e., sins, evil deeds, or wrongdoing towards others.

verses.translation: All faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, Self-Sustaining. Those burdened with wrongdoing[1] will be in a total loss.

verses.arabic: وَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَا يَخَافُ ظُلْمًا وَلَا هَضْمًا

english_rwwad.text: But whoever does righteous deeds, being a believer, will have no fear of being wronged or deprived.

verses.translation: But whoever does righteous deeds, being a believer, will have no fear of being wronged or deprived.

verses.arabic: وَكَذَٰلِكَ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ قُرْءَانًا عَرَبِيًّا وَصَرَّفْنَا فِيهِ مِنَ ٱلْوَعِيدِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ أَوْ يُحْدِثُ لَهُمْ ذِكْرًا

english_rwwad.text: We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur’an and diversified its warnings, so that they may fear Allah or it may cause them to take heed.

verses.translation: We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur’an and diversified its warnings, so that they may fear Allah or it may cause them to take heed.

verses.arabic: فَتَعَٰلَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمَلِكُ ٱلْحَقُّ وَلَا تَعْجَلْ بِٱلْقُرْءَانِ مِن قَبْلِ أَن يُقْضَىٰٓ إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُۥ وَقُل رَّبِّ زِدْنِى عِلْمًا

english_rwwad.text: So Exalted is Allah, the True Sovereign[1]. Do not hasten to [recite] the Qur’an before its revelation to you is concluded[2], and say, “My Lord, increase me in knowledge.”
english_rwwad.footnotes:
[1] Of everything in existence.
 [2] Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) was eager to recite the Qur’an while it was being revealed, so Allah Almighty told him to avoid being in haste in order to learn them before the verses are properly delivered; rather, listen to them attentively.

verses.translation: So Exalted is Allah, the True Sovereign[1]. Do not hasten to [recite] the Qur’an before its revelation to you is concluded[2], and say, “My Lord, increase me in knowledge.”

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ عَهِدْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ ءَادَمَ مِن قَبْلُ فَنَسِىَ وَلَمْ نَجِدْ لَهُۥ عَزْمًا

english_rwwad.text: We had already given a command to Adam before, but he forgot, and We found him lacking a firm resolve[1].
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] To resist the temptation of eating from the forbidden tree.

verses.translation: We had already given a command to Adam before, but he forgot, and We found him lacking a firm resolve[1].

verses.arabic: وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِـَٔادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ أَبَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: When We said to the angels, “Prostrate before Adam,” they all prostrated, except Iblīs[1], who refused.
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] See footnote 2:34.

verses.translation: When We said to the angels, “Prostrate before Adam,” they all prostrated, except Iblīs[1], who refused.

verses.arabic: فَقُلْنَا يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ إِنَّ هَٰذَا عَدُوٌّ لَّكَ وَلِزَوْجِكَ فَلَا يُخْرِجَنَّكُمَا مِنَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ فَتَشْقَىٰٓ

english_rwwad.text: We said “O Adam, this is an enemy to you and to your wife, so do not let him drive you both out of Paradise, for then you will fall into misery.

verses.translation: We said “O Adam, this is an enemy to you and to your wife, so do not let him drive you both out of Paradise, for then you will fall into misery.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ لَكَ أَلَّا تَجُوعَ فِيهَا وَلَا تَعْرَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: Here you will neither go hungry nor naked,

verses.translation: Here you will neither go hungry nor naked,

verses.arabic: وَأَنَّكَ لَا تَظْمَؤُا۟ فِيهَا وَلَا تَضْحَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: nor will you suffer from thirst or from scorching heat.”

verses.translation: nor will you suffer from thirst or from scorching heat.”

verses.arabic: فَوَسْوَسَ إِلَيْهِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَىٰ شَجَرَةِ ٱلْخُلْدِ وَمُلْكٍ لَّا يَبْلَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: Then Satan whispered to him, and said, “O Adam, shall I show you the tree of immortality and a kingdom that will never decay?”

verses.translation: Then Satan whispered to him, and said, “O Adam, shall I show you the tree of immortality and a kingdom that will never decay?”

verses.arabic: فَأَكَلَا مِنْهَا فَبَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْءَٰتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلْجَنَّةِ وَعَصَىٰٓ ءَادَمُ رَبَّهُۥ فَغَوَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: So they both ate from the tree, then their nakedness was revealed to each other, and they began to put together leaves from Paradise to cover themselves. Thus Adam disobeyed his Lord and fell into error[1].
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] Unlike the Bible, the Qur’an does not put the blame on Eve for Adam’s sin, for which they were ousted from the Garden and sent down to the earth. See: (Genesis 3).

verses.translation: So they both ate from the tree, then their nakedness was revealed to each other, and they began to put together leaves from Paradise to cover themselves. Thus Adam disobeyed his Lord and fell into error[1].

verses.arabic: ثُمَّ ٱجْتَبَٰهُ رَبُّهُۥ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ وَهَدَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: Thereafter his Lord chose him, accepted his repentance, and guided him.

verses.translation: Thereafter his Lord chose him, accepted his repentance, and guided him.

verses.arabic: قَالَ ٱهْبِطَا مِنْهَا جَمِيعًۢا بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًى فَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: Allah said, “Get down, both of you, from here altogether [with Satan] as enemies to one another. Then when there comes to you guidance from Me, whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor fall into misery[1].
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] Neither go astray (in this life) nor fall into misery (in the Hereafter).

verses.translation: Allah said, “Get down, both of you, from here altogether [with Satan] as enemies to one another. Then when there comes to you guidance from Me, whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor fall into misery[1].

verses.arabic: وَمَنْ أَعْرَضَ عَن ذِكْرِى فَإِنَّ لَهُۥ مَعِيشَةً ضَنكًا وَنَحْشُرُهُۥ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ أَعْمَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: But whoever turns away from My Reminder[1] will have a miserable life, and on the Day of Resurrection We will raise him blind.”
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] i.e., the Qur’an.

verses.translation: But whoever turns away from My Reminder[1] will have a miserable life, and on the Day of Resurrection We will raise him blind.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ رَبِّ لِمَ حَشَرْتَنِىٓ أَعْمَىٰ وَقَدْ كُنتُ بَصِيرًا

english_rwwad.text: He will say, “My Lord, why have you raised me blind when I was able to see before?”

verses.translation: He will say, “My Lord, why have you raised me blind when I was able to see before?”

verses.arabic: قَالَ كَذَٰلِكَ أَتَتْكَ ءَايَٰتُنَا فَنَسِيتَهَا وَكَذَٰلِكَ ٱلْيَوْمَ تُنسَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: Allah will say, “Similarly Our verses came to you, but you ignored them, so you will be ignored Today.”

verses.translation: Allah will say, “Similarly Our verses came to you, but you ignored them, so you will be ignored Today.”

verses.arabic: وَكَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى مَنْ أَسْرَفَ وَلَمْ يُؤْمِنۢ بِـَٔايَٰتِ رَبِّهِۦ وَلَعَذَابُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ أَشَدُّ وَأَبْقَىٰٓ

english_rwwad.text: This is how We recompense those who transgress the limits and do not believe in the verses of his Lord; and the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting[1].
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] Than that of the worldly life.

verses.translation: This is how We recompense those who transgress the limits and do not believe in the verses of his Lord; and the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting[1].

verses.arabic: أَفَلَمْ يَهْدِ لَهُمْ كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُم مِّنَ ٱلْقُرُونِ يَمْشُونَ فِى مَسَٰكِنِهِمْ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَـَٔايَٰتٍ لِّأُو۟لِى ٱلنُّهَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: Is it not yet clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them, in whose dwellings they still walk about? There are signs in this for people of sound intellect.

verses.translation: Is it not yet clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them, in whose dwellings they still walk about? There are signs in this for people of sound intellect.

verses.arabic: وَلَوْلَا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِن رَّبِّكَ لَكَانَ لِزَامًا وَأَجَلٌ مُّسَمًّى

english_rwwad.text: Were it not for a prior decree from your Lord[1] [O Prophet] and a time already set, they would have already been punished[2].
english_rwwad.footnotes:
[1] That He will not punish until the argument is established on them on the Day of Judgment.
 [2] He would have punished the disbelievers in the life of this world as He did with the destroyed nations of the past.

verses.translation: Were it not for a prior decree from your Lord[1] [O Prophet] and a time already set, they would have already been punished[2].

verses.arabic: فَٱصْبِرْ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ ٱلشَّمْسِ وَقَبْلَ غُرُوبِهَا وَمِنْ ءَانَآئِ ٱلَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْ وَأَطْرَافَ ٱلنَّهَارِ لَعَلَّكَ تَرْضَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: So be patient with what they say, and glorify your Lord with praise before sunrise and before sunset, and glorify Him during the night and at both ends of the day, so that you may be pleased [with the reward].

verses.translation: So be patient with what they say, and glorify your Lord with praise before sunrise and before sunset, and glorify Him during the night and at both ends of the day, so that you may be pleased [with the reward].

verses.arabic: وَلَا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ إِلَىٰ مَا مَتَّعْنَا بِهِۦٓ أَزْوَٰجًا مِّنْهُمْ زَهْرَةَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ فِيهِ وَرِزْقُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: Do not turn your eyes covetously towards the various forms of splendor of this life that We have given some of the [disbelievers] to enjoy, as a trial for them. But the provision of your Lord is far better and more lasting.

verses.translation: Do not turn your eyes covetously towards the various forms of splendor of this life that We have given some of the [disbelievers] to enjoy, as a trial for them. But the provision of your Lord is far better and more lasting.

verses.arabic: وَأْمُرْ أَهْلَكَ بِٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَٱصْطَبِرْ عَلَيْهَا لَا نَسْـَٔلُكَ رِزْقًا نَّحْنُ نَرْزُقُكَ وَٱلْعَٰقِبَةُ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: Enjoin your household to perform prayer and adhere to it firmly. We ask no provision from you; rather, it is We Who give you provision. And the best outcome is for those who fear Allah.

verses.translation: Enjoin your household to perform prayer and adhere to it firmly. We ask no provision from you; rather, it is We Who give you provision. And the best outcome is for those who fear Allah.

verses.arabic: وَقَالُوا۟ لَوْلَا يَأْتِينَا بِـَٔايَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦٓ أَوَلَمْ تَأْتِهِم بَيِّنَةُ مَا فِى ٱلصُّحُفِ ٱلْأُولَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: They say, “Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?” Has there not come to them [the Qur’an as] a confirmation of what is in the earlier Scriptures[1]?
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] Concerning Muhammad’s prophethood and the Qur'an as a lasting miracle.

verses.translation: They say, “Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?” Has there not come to them [the Qur’an as] a confirmation of what is in the earlier Scriptures[1]?

verses.arabic: وَلَوْ أَنَّآ أَهْلَكْنَٰهُم بِعَذَابٍ مِّن قَبْلِهِۦ لَقَالُوا۟ رَبَّنَا لَوْلَآ أَرْسَلْتَ إِلَيْنَا رَسُولًا فَنَتَّبِعَ ءَايَٰتِكَ مِن قَبْلِ أَن نَّذِلَّ وَنَخْزَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: If We had destroyed them with a punishment before this[1], they would have said, “Our Lord, if only You had sent us a messenger so that we would have followed Your verses before being humiliated and disgraced.”
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] Before sending Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) or before sending the Qur’an.

verses.translation: If We had destroyed them with a punishment before this[1], they would have said, “Our Lord, if only You had sent us a messenger so that we would have followed Your verses before being humiliated and disgraced.”

verses.arabic: قُلْ كُلٌّ مُّتَرَبِّصٌ فَتَرَبَّصُوا۟ فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ أَصْحَٰبُ ٱلصِّرَٰطِ ٱلسَّوِىِّ وَمَنِ ٱهْتَدَىٰ

english_rwwad.text: Say, “Each of us is waiting[1], so wait! You will come to know who are the people of the straight path and who are rightly guided.”
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] For the end result of this matter.

verses.translation: Say, “Each of us is waiting[1], so wait! You will come to know who are the people of the straight path and who are rightly guided.”

verses.arabic: بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ ٱقْتَرَبَ لِلنَّاسِ حِسَابُهُمْ وَهُمْ فِى غَفْلَةٍ مُّعْرِضُونَ

english_rwwad.text: The reckoning of the people has drawn near, yet they are turning away heedlessly.

verses.translation: The reckoning of the people has drawn near, yet they are turning away heedlessly.

verses.arabic: مَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن ذِكْرٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِم مُّحْدَثٍ إِلَّا ٱسْتَمَعُوهُ وَهُمْ يَلْعَبُونَ

english_rwwad.text: Whenever new revelation comes to them from their Lord, they listen to it in jest,

verses.translation: Whenever new revelation comes to them from their Lord, they listen to it in jest,

verses.arabic: لَاهِيَةً قُلُوبُهُمْ وَأَسَرُّوا۟ ٱلنَّجْوَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ هَلْ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ أَفَتَأْتُونَ ٱلسِّحْرَ وَأَنتُمْ تُبْصِرُونَ

english_rwwad.text: with their hearts heedless. The wrongdoers whisper to one another in secret, “Is this but a human being just like yourselves? Will you then follow his magic, although you openly see?”

verses.translation: with their hearts heedless. The wrongdoers whisper to one another in secret, “Is this but a human being just like yourselves? Will you then follow his magic, although you openly see?”

verses.arabic: قَالَ رَبِّى يَعْلَمُ ٱلْقَوْلَ فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ

english_rwwad.text: He said, “My Lord knows every word spoken in the heavens and earth, for He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.”

verses.translation: He said, “My Lord knows every word spoken in the heavens and earth, for He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.”

verses.arabic: بَلْ قَالُوٓا۟ أَضْغَٰثُ أَحْلَٰمٍۭ بَلِ ٱفْتَرَىٰهُ بَلْ هُوَ شَاعِرٌ فَلْيَأْتِنَا بِـَٔايَةٍ كَمَآ أُرْسِلَ ٱلْأَوَّلُونَ

english_rwwad.text: Yet they say, “This [Qur’an] is a set of jumbled dreams! Rather, he has fabricated it! Rather, he is a poet! So let him bring us a sign just as the earlier messengers were sent with[1].”
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] Such as the staff of Moses (عليه السلام), the camel of Salih (عليه السلام) and the like.

verses.translation: Yet they say, “This [Qur’an] is a set of jumbled dreams! Rather, he has fabricated it! Rather, he is a poet! So let him bring us a sign just as the earlier messengers were sent with[1].”

verses.arabic: مَآ ءَامَنَتْ قَبْلَهُم مِّن قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَٰهَآ أَفَهُمْ يُؤْمِنُونَ

english_rwwad.text: Not a single town We destroyed before them had believed[1]. Will they then believe?
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] Although they witnessed signs and miracles.

verses.translation: Not a single town We destroyed before them had believed[1]. Will they then believe?

verses.arabic: وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا قَبْلَكَ إِلَّا رِجَالًا نُّوحِىٓ إِلَيْهِمْ فَسْـَٔلُوٓا۟ أَهْلَ ٱلذِّكْرِ إِن كُنتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ

english_rwwad.text: We did not send before you [O Prophet] except men to whom We gave a revelation, so [O people] ask the People of the Scriptures if you do not know.

verses.translation: We did not send before you [O Prophet] except men to whom We gave a revelation, so [O people] ask the People of the Scriptures if you do not know.

verses.arabic: وَمَا جَعَلْنَٰهُمْ جَسَدًا لَّا يَأْكُلُونَ ٱلطَّعَامَ وَمَا كَانُوا۟ خَٰلِدِينَ

english_rwwad.text: We did not give them bodies that needed no food[1], nor were they immortal.
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] Such as the angels.

verses.translation: We did not give them bodies that needed no food[1], nor were they immortal.

verses.arabic: ثُمَّ صَدَقْنَٰهُمُ ٱلْوَعْدَ فَأَنجَيْنَٰهُمْ وَمَن نَّشَآءُ وَأَهْلَكْنَا ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ

english_rwwad.text: Then We fulfilled Our promise to them: We saved them[1] and those whom We willed, and destroyed those who transgressed all bounds.
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] After they conveyed the message.

verses.translation: Then We fulfilled Our promise to them: We saved them[1] and those whom We willed, and destroyed those who transgressed all bounds.

verses.arabic: لَقَدْ أَنزَلْنَآ إِلَيْكُمْ كِتَٰبًا فِيهِ ذِكْرُكُمْ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ

english_rwwad.text: We have sent down to you [O people] a Book in which there is honor for you[1]. Do you not then understand?
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] As you have been mentioned and addressed in the Qur’an, or there is a reminder for you in it.

verses.translation: We have sent down to you [O people] a Book in which there is honor for you[1]. Do you not then understand?

verses.arabic: وَكَمْ قَصَمْنَا مِن قَرْيَةٍ كَانَتْ ظَالِمَةً وَأَنشَأْنَا بَعْدَهَا قَوْمًا ءَاخَرِينَ

english_rwwad.text: [Imagine] how many towns of wrongdoers We have destroyed[1], and raised after them another people!
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] i.e., who were persisting in wrongdoing.

verses.translation: [Imagine] how many towns of wrongdoers We have destroyed[1], and raised after them another people!

verses.arabic: فَلَمَّآ أَحَسُّوا۟ بَأْسَنَآ إِذَا هُم مِّنْهَا يَرْكُضُونَ

english_rwwad.text: When they sensed Our punishment, they started running away from it.

verses.translation: When they sensed Our punishment, they started running away from it.

verses.arabic: لَا تَرْكُضُوا۟ وَٱرْجِعُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ مَآ أُتْرِفْتُمْ فِيهِ وَمَسَٰكِنِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُسْـَٔلُونَ

english_rwwad.text: “Do not run away, but return to your luxuries and dwellings[1], perhaps you will be questioned.”
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] This is said to them in sarcasm and ridicule.

verses.translation: “Do not run away, but return to your luxuries and dwellings[1], perhaps you will be questioned.”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ يَٰوَيْلَنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَٰلِمِينَ

english_rwwad.text: They said, “Woe to us! We were indeed wrongdoers.”

verses.translation: They said, “Woe to us! We were indeed wrongdoers.”

verses.arabic: فَمَا زَالَت تِّلْكَ دَعْوَىٰهُمْ حَتَّىٰ جَعَلْنَٰهُمْ حَصِيدًا خَٰمِدِينَ

english_rwwad.text: They kept crying this out loud until We mowed them down, lifeless[1].
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] i.e., extinguished like ashes.

verses.translation: They kept crying this out loud until We mowed them down, lifeless[1].

verses.arabic: وَمَا خَلَقْنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا لَٰعِبِينَ

english_rwwad.text: We did not create the heavens and earth and all that is between them for fun.

verses.translation: We did not create the heavens and earth and all that is between them for fun.

verses.arabic: لَوْ أَرَدْنَآ أَن نَّتَّخِذَ لَهْوًا لَّٱتَّخَذْنَٰهُ مِن لَّدُنَّآ إِن كُنَّا فَٰعِلِينَ

english_rwwad.text: If We had wished for a pastime[1], We could have had it from Our own, if We were to do so.
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] Such as a wife or a child.

verses.translation: If We had wished for a pastime[1], We could have had it from Our own, if We were to do so.

verses.arabic: بَلْ نَقْذِفُ بِٱلْحَقِّ عَلَى ٱلْبَٰطِلِ فَيَدْمَغُهُۥ فَإِذَا هُوَ زَاهِقٌ وَلَكُمُ ٱلْوَيْلُ مِمَّا تَصِفُونَ

english_rwwad.text: Rather, We hurl the truth at falsehood, and it crushes it[1], so it vanishes. Woe to you for what you falsely ascribe [to Allah][2]!
english_rwwad.footnotes:
[1] Lit. "strikes its brain," disabling or killing it.
 [2] Claiming that He has a son, a wife, or a partner.

verses.translation: Rather, We hurl the truth at falsehood, and it crushes it[1], so it vanishes. Woe to you for what you falsely ascribe [to Allah][2]!

verses.arabic: وَلَهُۥ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَنْ عِندَهُۥ لَا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِهِۦ وَلَا يَسْتَحْسِرُونَ

english_rwwad.text: To Him belongs all those who are in the heavens and earth. Those [angels] who are with Him are not too proud to worship Him, nor do they ever grow weary.

verses.translation: To Him belongs all those who are in the heavens and earth. Those [angels] who are with Him are not too proud to worship Him, nor do they ever grow weary.

verses.arabic: يُسَبِّحُونَ ٱلَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ لَا يَفْتُرُونَ

english_rwwad.text: They glorify Him day and night tirelessly.

verses.translation: They glorify Him day and night tirelessly.

verses.arabic: أَمِ ٱتَّخَذُوٓا۟ ءَالِهَةً مِّنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ هُمْ يُنشِرُونَ

english_rwwad.text: Or have they taken gods from the earth who [cannot even] resurrect the dead?

verses.translation: Or have they taken gods from the earth who [cannot even] resurrect the dead?

verses.arabic: لَوْ كَانَ فِيهِمَآ ءَالِهَةٌ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتَا فَسُبْحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَرْشِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ

english_rwwad.text: If there had been gods besides Allah in the heavens and earth, both realms would have fallen in disorder. Glory be to Allah – Lord of the Throne – far above what they ascribe [to Him].

verses.translation: If there had been gods besides Allah in the heavens and earth, both realms would have fallen in disorder. Glory be to Allah – Lord of the Throne – far above what they ascribe [to Him].

verses.arabic: لَا يُسْـَٔلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وَهُمْ يُسْـَٔلُونَ

english_rwwad.text: He cannot be questioned for what He does, but they will be questioned.

verses.translation: He cannot be questioned for what He does, but they will be questioned.

verses.arabic: أَمِ ٱتَّخَذُوا۟ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ ءَالِهَةً قُلْ هَاتُوا۟ بُرْهَٰنَكُمْ هَٰذَا ذِكْرُ مَن مَّعِىَ وَذِكْرُ مَن قَبْلِى بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ ٱلْحَقَّ فَهُم مُّعْرِضُونَ

english_rwwad.text: Or have they taken other gods besides Him? Say, “Bring your proof. Here is the Book of those who are with me, and the Book of those who came before me[1].” Yet most of them do not know the truth, so they turn away.
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] The Prophet (ﷺ) is addressed to challenge the pagans to produce their proof for the existence of other gods; whereas, the Qur’an, the Torah, and the Gospel are in agreement that there is no god but Allah alone.

verses.translation: Or have they taken other gods besides Him? Say, “Bring your proof. Here is the Book of those who are with me, and the Book of those who came before me[1].” Yet most of them do not know the truth, so they turn away.

verses.arabic: وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا نُوحِىٓ إِلَيْهِ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنَا۠ فَٱعْبُدُونِ

english_rwwad.text: “We never sent before you [O Prophet] any messenger without revealing to him that none has the right to be worshiped except Me, so worship Me.”

verses.translation: “We never sent before you [O Prophet] any messenger without revealing to him that none has the right to be worshiped except Me, so worship Me.”

verses.arabic: وَقَالُوا۟ ٱتَّخَذَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ وَلَدًا سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ بَلْ عِبَادٌ مُّكْرَمُونَ

english_rwwad.text: They say, “The Most Compassionate has begotten offspring!”[1] Glory be to Him! In fact, those [angels] are His honored slaves.
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] The pagans claimed that angels are the daughters of Allah.

verses.translation: They say, “The Most Compassionate has begotten offspring!”[1] Glory be to Him! In fact, those [angels] are His honored slaves.

verses.arabic: لَا يَسْبِقُونَهُۥ بِٱلْقَوْلِ وَهُم بِأَمْرِهِۦ يَعْمَلُونَ

english_rwwad.text: They do not speak before He speaks, and they only do as He commands.

verses.translation: They do not speak before He speaks, and they only do as He commands.

verses.arabic: يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ وَلَا يَشْفَعُونَ إِلَّا لِمَنِ ٱرْتَضَىٰ وَهُم مِّنْ خَشْيَتِهِۦ مُشْفِقُونَ

english_rwwad.text: He knows what is ahead of them and what is behind them[1]. They cannot intercede except for whom He pleases, and they are fearful in awe of Him.
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] See footnote 2:255.

verses.translation: He knows what is ahead of them and what is behind them[1]. They cannot intercede except for whom He pleases, and they are fearful in awe of Him.

verses.arabic: وَمَن يَقُلْ مِنْهُمْ إِنِّىٓ إِلَٰهٌ مِّن دُونِهِۦ فَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِيهِ جَهَنَّمَ كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

english_rwwad.text: If anyone of them were to say, “I am god besides Him,” We would punish him with Hell. This is how We punish the wrongdoers.

verses.translation: If anyone of them were to say, “I am god besides Him,” We would punish him with Hell. This is how We punish the wrongdoers.

verses.arabic: أَوَلَمْ يَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقًا فَفَتَقْنَٰهُمَا وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ حَىٍّ أَفَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ

english_rwwad.text: Are the disbelievers not aware that the heavens and earth were joined together and then We split them apart? We created from water every living thing. Will they not then believe?

verses.translation: Are the disbelievers not aware that the heavens and earth were joined together and then We split them apart? We created from water every living thing. Will they not then believe?

verses.arabic: وَجَعَلْنَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ رَوَٰسِىَ أَن تَمِيدَ بِهِمْ وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا فِجَاجًا سُبُلًا لَّعَلَّهُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ

english_rwwad.text: We have set on the earth firm mountains so it does not shake with them, and We have made therein broad pathways so that they may find their way.

verses.translation: We have set on the earth firm mountains so it does not shake with them, and We have made therein broad pathways so that they may find their way.

verses.arabic: وَجَعَلْنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ سَقْفًا مَّحْفُوظًا وَهُمْ عَنْ ءَايَٰتِهَا مُعْرِضُونَ

english_rwwad.text: And We have made the sky a well-protected canopy, yet they turn away from its signs[1].
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] Such as the sun and the moon.

verses.translation: And We have made the sky a well-protected canopy, yet they turn away from its signs[1].

verses.arabic: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ وَٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ كُلٌّ فِى فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ

english_rwwad.text: It is He Who created the night and the day, the sun and the moon – each floating in its orbit.

verses.translation: It is He Who created the night and the day, the sun and the moon – each floating in its orbit.

verses.arabic: وَمَا جَعَلْنَا لِبَشَرٍ مِّن قَبْلِكَ ٱلْخُلْدَ أَفَإِي۟ن مِّتَّ فَهُمُ ٱلْخَٰلِدُونَ

english_rwwad.text: We did not grant immortality to any human being before you [O Prophet]. So if you die, will they live forever?

verses.translation: We did not grant immortality to any human being before you [O Prophet]. So if you die, will they live forever?

verses.arabic: كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَآئِقَةُ ٱلْمَوْتِ وَنَبْلُوكُم بِٱلشَّرِّ وَٱلْخَيْرِ فِتْنَةً وَإِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ

english_rwwad.text: Every soul will taste death; We test you with bad and good as a trial, then to Us you will all be returned.

verses.translation: Every soul will taste death; We test you with bad and good as a trial, then to Us you will all be returned.

verses.arabic: وَإِذَا رَءَاكَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ إِن يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إِلَّا هُزُوًا أَهَٰذَا ٱلَّذِى يَذْكُرُ ءَالِهَتَكُمْ وَهُم بِذِكْرِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ هُمْ كَٰفِرُونَ

english_rwwad.text: When the disbelievers see you, they only take you in ridicule, [saying], “Is this the one who speaks ill of your gods?” while they reject even the mention of the Most Compassionate.

verses.translation: When the disbelievers see you, they only take you in ridicule, [saying], “Is this the one who speaks ill of your gods?” while they reject even the mention of the Most Compassionate.

verses.arabic: خُلِقَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ مِنْ عَجَلٍ سَأُو۟رِيكُمْ ءَايَٰتِى فَلَا تَسْتَعْجِلُونِ

english_rwwad.text: Man is created of haste. I will show you My signs, so do not ask Me to hasten them.

verses.translation: Man is created of haste. I will show you My signs, so do not ask Me to hasten them.

verses.arabic: وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هَٰذَا ٱلْوَعْدُ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ

english_rwwad.text: They say, “When will this promise come to pass, if you are truthful?”

verses.translation: They say, “When will this promise come to pass, if you are truthful?”

verses.arabic: لَوْ يَعْلَمُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ حِينَ لَا يَكُفُّونَ عَن وُجُوهِهِمُ ٱلنَّارَ وَلَا عَن ظُهُورِهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ

english_rwwad.text: If only the disbelievers knew the moment when they would be unable to ward the Fire off their faces or their backs, nor would they be helped[1].
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] The completion of the sentence is "...they would not be asking for the punishment."

verses.translation: If only the disbelievers knew the moment when they would be unable to ward the Fire off their faces or their backs, nor would they be helped[1].

verses.arabic: بَلْ تَأْتِيهِم بَغْتَةً فَتَبْهَتُهُمْ فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ رَدَّهَا وَلَا هُمْ يُنظَرُونَ

english_rwwad.text: Rather, it will come upon them suddenly and stun them; they will not be able to avert it, nor will they be given respite.

verses.translation: Rather, it will come upon them suddenly and stun them; they will not be able to avert it, nor will they be given respite.

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدِ ٱسْتُهْزِئَ بِرُسُلٍ مِّن قَبْلِكَ فَحَاقَ بِٱلَّذِينَ سَخِرُوا۟ مِنْهُم مَّا كَانُوا۟ بِهِۦ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ

english_rwwad.text: Indeed, there were messengers before you who were ridiculed, but those who mocked them were encompassed by what they used to ridicule.

verses.translation: Indeed, there were messengers before you who were ridiculed, but those who mocked them were encompassed by what they used to ridicule.

verses.arabic: قُلْ مَن يَكْلَؤُكُم بِٱلَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ مِنَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ بَلْ هُمْ عَن ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِم مُّعْرِضُونَ

english_rwwad.text: Say, “Who can protect you by night and by day against the Most Compassionate?” Yet they turn away from the admonition of their Lord.

verses.translation: Say, “Who can protect you by night and by day against the Most Compassionate?” Yet they turn away from the admonition of their Lord.

verses.arabic: أَمْ لَهُمْ ءَالِهَةٌ تَمْنَعُهُم مِّن دُونِنَا لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ نَصْرَ أَنفُسِهِمْ وَلَا هُم مِّنَّا يُصْحَبُونَ

english_rwwad.text: Do they have gods who can defend them against Us? They cannot even help themselves, nor will they be protected from Us.

verses.translation: Do they have gods who can defend them against Us? They cannot even help themselves, nor will they be protected from Us.

verses.arabic: بَلْ مَتَّعْنَا هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ وَءَابَآءَهُمْ حَتَّىٰ طَالَ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْعُمُرُ أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَنَّا نَأْتِى ٱلْأَرْضَ نَنقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَآ أَفَهُمُ ٱلْغَٰلِبُونَ

english_rwwad.text: Nevertheless, We have provided for them and their forefathers luxuries which they enjoyed for a long time. Do they not see that We gradually reduce the land from its outlying sides?[1] Is it they who will then prevail?
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] See footnote 13:41.

verses.translation: Nevertheless, We have provided for them and their forefathers luxuries which they enjoyed for a long time. Do they not see that We gradually reduce the land from its outlying sides?[1] Is it they who will then prevail?

verses.arabic: قُلْ إِنَّمَآ أُنذِرُكُم بِٱلْوَحْىِ وَلَا يَسْمَعُ ٱلصُّمُّ ٱلدُّعَآءَ إِذَا مَا يُنذَرُونَ

english_rwwad.text: Say, “I only warn you by divine revelation.” But the deaf cannot hear the call when they are warned.

verses.translation: Say, “I only warn you by divine revelation.” But the deaf cannot hear the call when they are warned.

verses.arabic: وَلَئِن مَّسَّتْهُمْ نَفْحَةٌ مِّنْ عَذَابِ رَبِّكَ لَيَقُولُنَّ يَٰوَيْلَنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَٰلِمِينَ

english_rwwad.text: If a mere breath of your Lord’s torment were to touch them, they would surely say, “Woe to us! We were indeed wrongdoers.”

verses.translation: If a mere breath of your Lord’s torment were to touch them, they would surely say, “Woe to us! We were indeed wrongdoers.”

verses.arabic: وَنَضَعُ ٱلْمَوَٰزِينَ ٱلْقِسْطَ لِيَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ فَلَا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌ شَيْـًٔا وَإِن كَانَ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ مِّنْ خَرْدَلٍ أَتَيْنَا بِهَا وَكَفَىٰ بِنَا حَٰسِبِينَ

english_rwwad.text: We will place the scales of justice on the Day of Resurrection, and no soul will be wronged in the least. Even if a deed is the weight of a mustard seed[1], We will bring it forth. Sufficient are We as Reckoners.
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] i.e., as small or insignificant as a mustard seed.

verses.translation: We will place the scales of justice on the Day of Resurrection, and no soul will be wronged in the least. Even if a deed is the weight of a mustard seed[1], We will bring it forth. Sufficient are We as Reckoners.

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ وَهَٰرُونَ ٱلْفُرْقَانَ وَضِيَآءً وَذِكْرًا لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ

english_rwwad.text: We certainly gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion, shining light and admonition[1] for the righteous,
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] These are Torah’s three qualities.

verses.translation: We certainly gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion, shining light and admonition[1] for the righteous,

verses.arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلْغَيْبِ وَهُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّاعَةِ مُشْفِقُونَ

english_rwwad.text: those who fear their Lord without seeing Him[1], and are apprehensive of the Hour.
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] Or when they are in private and not seen by others.

verses.translation: those who fear their Lord without seeing Him[1], and are apprehensive of the Hour.

verses.arabic: وَهَٰذَا ذِكْرٌ مُّبَارَكٌ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ أَفَأَنتُمْ لَهُۥ مُنكِرُونَ

english_rwwad.text: And this [Qur’an] is a blessed reminder which We have sent down. Are you still denying it[1]?
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] i.e., pretending ignorance or refusing to acknowledge it?

verses.translation: And this [Qur’an] is a blessed reminder which We have sent down. Are you still denying it[1]?

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَآ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ رُشْدَهُۥ مِن قَبْلُ وَكُنَّا بِهِۦ عَٰلِمِينَ

english_rwwad.text: Indeed, We had given Abraham sound judgment before[1], for We know him well.
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] i.e., before Moses, or in his early youth.

verses.translation: Indeed, We had given Abraham sound judgment before[1], for We know him well.

verses.arabic: إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِۦ مَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلتَّمَاثِيلُ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنتُمْ لَهَا عَٰكِفُونَ

english_rwwad.text: When he said to his father and his people, “What are these statues to which you are so devoted?”

verses.translation: When he said to his father and his people, “What are these statues to which you are so devoted?”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ وَجَدْنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا لَهَا عَٰبِدِينَ

english_rwwad.text: They said, “We found our forefathers worshiping them.”

verses.translation: They said, “We found our forefathers worshiping them.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ لَقَدْ كُنتُمْ أَنتُمْ وَءَابَآؤُكُمْ فِى ضَلَٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ

english_rwwad.text: He said, “Indeed, you and your forefathers were clearly misguided.”

verses.translation: He said, “Indeed, you and your forefathers were clearly misguided.”

verses.arabic: قَالُوٓا۟ أَجِئْتَنَا بِٱلْحَقِّ أَمْ أَنتَ مِنَ ٱللَّٰعِبِينَ

english_rwwad.text: They said, “Have you come to us with the truth, or are you joking?”

verses.translation: They said, “Have you come to us with the truth, or are you joking?”

verses.arabic: قَالَ بَل رَّبُّكُمْ رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلَّذِى فَطَرَهُنَّ وَأَنَا۠ عَلَىٰ ذَٰلِكُم مِّنَ ٱلشَّٰهِدِينَ

english_rwwad.text: He said, “Nay, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and earth, Who created them, and I am one of those who bear witness to it.

verses.translation: He said, “Nay, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and earth, Who created them, and I am one of those who bear witness to it.

verses.arabic: وَتَٱللَّهِ لَأَكِيدَنَّ أَصْنَٰمَكُم بَعْدَ أَن تُوَلُّوا۟ مُدْبِرِينَ

english_rwwad.text: By Allah, I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned and gone away.”

verses.translation: By Allah, I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned and gone away.”

verses.arabic: فَجَعَلَهُمْ جُذَٰذًا إِلَّا كَبِيرًا لَّهُمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِ يَرْجِعُونَ

english_rwwad.text: So he broke them into pieces, except the biggest of them, so that they might come back to it.

verses.translation: So he broke them into pieces, except the biggest of them, so that they might come back to it.

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ مَن فَعَلَ هَٰذَا بِـَٔالِهَتِنَآ إِنَّهُۥ لَمِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

english_rwwad.text: They said, “Who has done this to our gods? He is indeed one of the wrongdoers.”

verses.translation: They said, “Who has done this to our gods? He is indeed one of the wrongdoers.”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ سَمِعْنَا فَتًى يَذْكُرُهُمْ يُقَالُ لَهُۥٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمُ

english_rwwad.text: They said, “We heard a young man, speaking ill of them, who is called Abraham.”

verses.translation: They said, “We heard a young man, speaking ill of them, who is called Abraham.”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ فَأْتُوا۟ بِهِۦ عَلَىٰٓ أَعْيُنِ ٱلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَشْهَدُونَ

english_rwwad.text: They said, “Bring him then before the eyes of the people, so that they may witness [his trial][1].”
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] Or his confession about what he did.

verses.translation: They said, “Bring him then before the eyes of the people, so that they may witness [his trial][1].”

verses.arabic: قَالُوٓا۟ ءَأَنتَ فَعَلْتَ هَٰذَا بِـَٔالِهَتِنَا يَٰٓإِبْرَٰهِيمُ

english_rwwad.text: They said, “Are you the one who did this to our gods, O Abraham?”

verses.translation: They said, “Are you the one who did this to our gods, O Abraham?”

verses.arabic: قَالَ بَلْ فَعَلَهُۥ كَبِيرُهُمْ هَٰذَا فَسْـَٔلُوهُمْ إِن كَانُوا۟ يَنطِقُونَ

english_rwwad.text: He said, “Rather, it was this biggest one who did it. So ask them, if they can speak!”

verses.translation: He said, “Rather, it was this biggest one who did it. So ask them, if they can speak!”

verses.arabic: فَرَجَعُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ فَقَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّكُمْ أَنتُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ

english_rwwad.text: So they turned back to one another, and said, “Indeed, it is you who are the wrongdoers.”

verses.translation: So they turned back to one another, and said, “Indeed, it is you who are the wrongdoers.”

verses.arabic: ثُمَّ نُكِسُوا۟ عَلَىٰ رُءُوسِهِمْ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَا هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ يَنطِقُونَ

english_rwwad.text: Then they turned to their obstinacy[1], [saying], “You already know that they cannot speak.”
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] After first admitting their error.

verses.translation: Then they turned to their obstinacy[1], [saying], “You already know that they cannot speak.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ أَفَتَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنفَعُكُمْ شَيْـًٔا وَلَا يَضُرُّكُمْ

english_rwwad.text: Abraham said, “Do you then worship besides Allah that which can neither benefit nor harm you in the least?

verses.translation: Abraham said, “Do you then worship besides Allah that which can neither benefit nor harm you in the least?

verses.arabic: أُفٍّ لَّكُمْ وَلِمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ

english_rwwad.text: Fie upon you[1] and upon all that you worship besides Allah! Do you not have any sense?”
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] An expression of anger and displeasure.

verses.translation: Fie upon you[1] and upon all that you worship besides Allah! Do you not have any sense?”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ حَرِّقُوهُ وَٱنصُرُوٓا۟ ءَالِهَتَكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ فَٰعِلِينَ

english_rwwad.text: They said, “Burn him and avenge your gods if you must do something.”

verses.translation: They said, “Burn him and avenge your gods if you must do something.”

verses.arabic: قُلْنَا يَٰنَارُ كُونِى بَرْدًا وَسَلَٰمًا عَلَىٰٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ

english_rwwad.text: We said, “O fire, be cool and safe for Abraham.”[1]
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] It is reported in an authentic Hadīth that Abraham said, while being thrown into the fire, “Allah is sufficient for us and He is the best Protector.”

verses.translation: We said, “O fire, be cool and safe for Abraham.”[1]

verses.arabic: وَأَرَادُوا۟ بِهِۦ كَيْدًا فَجَعَلْنَٰهُمُ ٱلْأَخْسَرِينَ

english_rwwad.text: They plotted to harm him, but We made them the worst losers.

verses.translation: They plotted to harm him, but We made them the worst losers.

verses.arabic: وَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ وَلُوطًا إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلَّتِى بَٰرَكْنَا فِيهَا لِلْعَٰلَمِينَ

english_rwwad.text: And We saved him and Lot [and brought him] to the land[1] that we have blessed for all people.
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] i.e., the Levant. Abraham and his nephew, Lot, were saved from their enemy Nimrod and his people, as they migrated from the land of Babel, Iraq to Jerusalem.

verses.translation: And We saved him and Lot [and brought him] to the land[1] that we have blessed for all people.

verses.arabic: وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُۥٓ إِسْحَٰقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ نَافِلَةً وَكُلًّا جَعَلْنَا صَٰلِحِينَ

english_rwwad.text: And We gave him Isaac, and then Jacob, a grandson, and We made all of them righteous.

verses.translation: And We gave him Isaac, and then Jacob, a grandson, and We made all of them righteous.

verses.arabic: وَجَعَلْنَٰهُمْ أَئِمَّةً يَهْدُونَ بِأَمْرِنَا وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِمْ فِعْلَ ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ وَإِقَامَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَإِيتَآءَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةِ وَكَانُوا۟ لَنَا عَٰبِدِينَ

english_rwwad.text: And We made them leaders, guiding people by Our command, and We inspired them to do righteous deeds, establish prayer and give zakah[1]; and they were Our true worshipers.
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] The term "zakah" denotes purification and growth.

verses.translation: And We made them leaders, guiding people by Our command, and We inspired them to do righteous deeds, establish prayer and give zakah[1]; and they were Our true worshipers.

verses.arabic: وَلُوطًا ءَاتَيْنَٰهُ حُكْمًا وَعِلْمًا وَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلْقَرْيَةِ ٱلَّتِى كَانَت تَّعْمَلُ ٱلْخَبَٰٓئِثَ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمَ سَوْءٍ فَٰسِقِينَ

english_rwwad.text: To Lot We gave sound judgment and knowledge, and We saved him from the town that was engrossed in shameful practices. They were Indeed an evil and rebellious people.

verses.translation: To Lot We gave sound judgment and knowledge, and We saved him from the town that was engrossed in shameful practices. They were Indeed an evil and rebellious people.

verses.arabic: وَأَدْخَلْنَٰهُ فِى رَحْمَتِنَآ إِنَّهُۥ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ

english_rwwad.text: And We admitted him to Our mercy, for he was one of the righteous.

verses.translation: And We admitted him to Our mercy, for he was one of the righteous.

verses.arabic: وَنُوحًا إِذْ نَادَىٰ مِن قَبْلُ فَٱسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُۥ فَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ وَأَهْلَهُۥ مِنَ ٱلْكَرْبِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ

english_rwwad.text: And [remember] Noah, when he called out[1] to Us before, so We responded to him and saved him and his household[2] from the great distress.
english_rwwad.footnotes:
[1] i.e., supplicated against his people who had persisted in denial.
 [2] i.e., the believers of his household.

verses.translation: And [remember] Noah, when he called out[1] to Us before, so We responded to him and saved him and his household[2] from the great distress.

verses.arabic: وَنَصَرْنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمَ سَوْءٍ فَأَغْرَقْنَٰهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ

english_rwwad.text: And We helped him against the people who rejected Our signs. They were indeed evil people, so We drowned them all.

verses.translation: And We helped him against the people who rejected Our signs. They were indeed evil people, so We drowned them all.

verses.arabic: وَدَاوُۥدَ وَسُلَيْمَٰنَ إِذْ يَحْكُمَانِ فِى ٱلْحَرْثِ إِذْ نَفَشَتْ فِيهِ غَنَمُ ٱلْقَوْمِ وَكُنَّا لِحُكْمِهِمْ شَٰهِدِينَ

english_rwwad.text: And [remember] David and Solomon, when they passed judgment about the tillage into which some people’s sheep had strayed at night[1], and We were witnesses to their judgment.
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] Destroying the crops and eating therefrom.

verses.translation: And [remember] David and Solomon, when they passed judgment about the tillage into which some people’s sheep had strayed at night[1], and We were witnesses to their judgment.

verses.arabic: فَفَهَّمْنَٰهَا سُلَيْمَٰنَ وَكُلًّا ءَاتَيْنَا حُكْمًا وَعِلْمًا وَسَخَّرْنَا مَعَ دَاوُۥدَ ٱلْجِبَالَ يُسَبِّحْنَ وَٱلطَّيْرَ وَكُنَّا فَٰعِلِينَ

english_rwwad.text: We made Solomon understand it[1], although We gave each of them sound judgment and knowledge. We subjected the mountains and birds to glorify Allah along with David. It was We Who did all this.
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] A man’s flock of sheep strayed into another man’s tillage. When the two men came to David for judgment, he ruled that the shepherd must give his sheep in compensation for the damage. Nonetheless, Solomon suggested that the sheep be kept with the owner of the tillage, so he may benefit from their milk and wool, while the shepherd should work on the land to restore it to its former state. Thus, the farmer would take back his tillage in perfect condition, and the sheep would be returned to its owner. David was impressed by his son’s insightful and fair judgment and approved it.

verses.translation: We made Solomon understand it[1], although We gave each of them sound judgment and knowledge. We subjected the mountains and birds to glorify Allah along with David. It was We Who did all this.

verses.arabic: وَعَلَّمْنَٰهُ صَنْعَةَ لَبُوسٍ لَّكُمْ لِتُحْصِنَكُم مِّنۢ بَأْسِكُمْ فَهَلْ أَنتُمْ شَٰكِرُونَ

english_rwwad.text: And We taught him[1] the art of making coats of mail for you to protect yourselves in your battle. Will you then be grateful?
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] i.e., David apart from Solomon.

verses.translation: And We taught him[1] the art of making coats of mail for you to protect yourselves in your battle. Will you then be grateful?

verses.arabic: وَلِسُلَيْمَٰنَ ٱلرِّيحَ عَاصِفَةً تَجْرِى بِأَمْرِهِۦٓ إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلَّتِى بَٰرَكْنَا فِيهَا وَكُنَّا بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَٰلِمِينَ

english_rwwad.text: And to Solomon [We subjected] the raging wind, to blow by his command to the land We had blessed. It is We Who have full knowledge of everything.

verses.translation: And to Solomon [We subjected] the raging wind, to blow by his command to the land We had blessed. It is We Who have full knowledge of everything.

verses.arabic: وَمِنَ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينِ مَن يَغُوصُونَ لَهُۥ وَيَعْمَلُونَ عَمَلًا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ وَكُنَّا لَهُمْ حَٰفِظِينَ

english_rwwad.text: And among the devils [We subjected] those who dived for him[1] and performed other duties. It is We Who were watching over them[2].
english_rwwad.footnotes:
[1] Bringing him pearls.
 [2] Preventing any disobedience from Solomon's instructions and protecting him from being harmed by them.

verses.translation: And among the devils [We subjected] those who dived for him[1] and performed other duties. It is We Who were watching over them[2].

verses.arabic: وَأَيُّوبَ إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥٓ أَنِّى مَسَّنِىَ ٱلضُّرُّ وَأَنتَ أَرْحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ

english_rwwad.text: And [remember] Job, when he cried out to his Lord, “I have been struck by adversity[1], and You are the Most Merciful of those who show mercy.”
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] i.e., loss of health, wealth, and children.

verses.translation: And [remember] Job, when he cried out to his Lord, “I have been struck by adversity[1], and You are the Most Merciful of those who show mercy.”

verses.arabic: فَٱسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُۥ فَكَشَفْنَا مَا بِهِۦ مِن ضُرٍّ وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُ أَهْلَهُۥ وَمِثْلَهُم مَّعَهُمْ رَحْمَةً مِّنْ عِندِنَا وَذِكْرَىٰ لِلْعَٰبِدِينَ

english_rwwad.text: So We responded to him and relieved his adversity, and We restored to him his family, twice as many, as a mercy from Us and as a reminder for Our worshipers.

verses.translation: So We responded to him and relieved his adversity, and We restored to him his family, twice as many, as a mercy from Us and as a reminder for Our worshipers.

verses.arabic: وَإِسْمَٰعِيلَ وَإِدْرِيسَ وَذَا ٱلْكِفْلِ كُلٌّ مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ

english_rwwad.text: And [remember] Ishmael, Idrīs and Dhul-Kifl[1]; they were all steadfast.
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] Idrīs (Enoch); Dhul-Kifl (Ezekiel, or Isaiah).

verses.translation: And [remember] Ishmael, Idrīs and Dhul-Kifl[1]; they were all steadfast.

verses.arabic: وَأَدْخَلْنَٰهُمْ فِى رَحْمَتِنَآ إِنَّهُم مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ

english_rwwad.text: And We admitted them to Our mercy, for they were truly righteous.

verses.translation: And We admitted them to Our mercy, for they were truly righteous.

verses.arabic: وَذَا ٱلنُّونِ إِذ ذَّهَبَ مُغَٰضِبًا فَظَنَّ أَن لَّن نَّقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ فَنَادَىٰ فِى ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ أَن لَّآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنتَ سُبْحَٰنَكَ إِنِّى كُنتُ مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

english_rwwad.text: And [remember] the Man of the Whale [i.e., Jonah] when he departed in anger[1], thinking that We would not take him to task. Then he cried out in the depths of darkness[2], “None has the right to be worshiped except You. Glory be to You! I have certainly done wrong”.
english_rwwad.footnotes:
[1] Due to the disbelief of his people.
 [2] The darkness of the night, the sea, and the whale's belly.

verses.translation: And [remember] the Man of the Whale [i.e., Jonah] when he departed in anger[1], thinking that We would not take him to task. Then he cried out in the depths of darkness[2], “None has the right to be worshiped except You. Glory be to You! I have certainly done wrong”.

verses.arabic: فَٱسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُۥ وَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلْغَمِّ وَكَذَٰلِكَ نُـۨجِى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ

english_rwwad.text: So We answered his prayer and rescued him from distress. This is how We rescue the believers.

verses.translation: So We answered his prayer and rescued him from distress. This is how We rescue the believers.

verses.arabic: وَزَكَرِيَّآ إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥ رَبِّ لَا تَذَرْنِى فَرْدًا وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ ٱلْوَٰرِثِينَ

english_rwwad.text: And [remember] Zachariah, when he cried out to his Lord, “My Lord, do not leave me childless, for You are the Best of Inheritors.”

verses.translation: And [remember] Zachariah, when he cried out to his Lord, “My Lord, do not leave me childless, for You are the Best of Inheritors.”

verses.arabic: فَٱسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُۥ وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُۥ يَحْيَىٰ وَأَصْلَحْنَا لَهُۥ زَوْجَهُۥٓ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ يُسَٰرِعُونَ فِى ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ وَيَدْعُونَنَا رَغَبًا وَرَهَبًا وَكَانُوا۟ لَنَا خَٰشِعِينَ

english_rwwad.text: So We answered his prayer and gave him John, and made his wife fertile. They used to hasten in doing good deeds and used to call upon Us with hope and fear, and they were humble before Us.

verses.translation: So We answered his prayer and gave him John, and made his wife fertile. They used to hasten in doing good deeds and used to call upon Us with hope and fear, and they were humble before Us.

verses.arabic: وَٱلَّتِىٓ أَحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَهَا فَنَفَخْنَا فِيهَا مِن رُّوحِنَا وَجَعَلْنَٰهَا وَٱبْنَهَآ ءَايَةً لِّلْعَٰلَمِينَ

english_rwwad.text: And [remember Mary] who guarded her chastity; We breathed in her [garment] through Our Spirit [Gabriel] and made her and her son a sign for all people.

verses.translation: And [remember Mary] who guarded her chastity; We breathed in her [garment] through Our Spirit [Gabriel] and made her and her son a sign for all people.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ هَٰذِهِۦٓ أُمَّتُكُمْ أُمَّةً وَٰحِدَةً وَأَنَا۠ رَبُّكُمْ فَٱعْبُدُونِ

english_rwwad.text: Indeed, this religion of yours is one religion, and I am your Lord, so worship Me alone.

verses.translation: Indeed, this religion of yours is one religion, and I am your Lord, so worship Me alone.

verses.arabic: وَتَقَطَّعُوٓا۟ أَمْرَهُم بَيْنَهُمْ كُلٌّ إِلَيْنَا رَٰجِعُونَ

english_rwwad.text: But people have divided themselves into sects, yet they will all return to Us.

verses.translation: But people have divided themselves into sects, yet they will all return to Us.

verses.arabic: فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَا كُفْرَانَ لِسَعْيِهِۦ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ كَٰتِبُونَ

english_rwwad.text: Whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer, his efforts will not be denied[1], for We are recording them all.
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] i.e., He will not be deprived of his due reward.

verses.translation: Whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer, his efforts will not be denied[1], for We are recording them all.

verses.arabic: وَحَرَٰمٌ عَلَىٰ قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَٰهَآ أَنَّهُمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ

english_rwwad.text: It is not possible for any town that We have destroyed to ever come back [to this world][1],
english_rwwad.footnotes: [1] To repent to Allah.

verses.translation: It is not possible for any town that We have destroyed to ever come back [to this world][1],

verses.arabic: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا فُتِحَتْ يَأْجُوجُ وَمَأْجُوجُ وَهُم مِّن كُلِّ حَدَبٍ يَنسِلُونَ

english_rwwad.text: until when Gog and Magog are let loose, swarming swiftly from every mound,

verses.translation: until when Gog and Magog are let loose, swarming swiftly from every mound,

verses.arabic: وَٱقْتَرَبَ ٱلْوَعْدُ ٱلْحَقُّ فَإِذَا هِىَ شَٰخِصَةٌ أَبْصَٰرُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ يَٰوَيْلَنَا قَدْ كُنَّا فِى غَفْلَةٍ مِّنْ هَٰذَا بَلْ كُنَّا ظَٰلِمِينَ

english_rwwad.text: when the True Promise[1] draws near, the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare in horror, [saying], “Woe to us! We were indeed heedless of this; nay, we were wrongdoers.”
